title: Foam core
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Tuesday. The backroom of Heceta Frame & Matting. Foam core, a dull utility knife, and the word 'racket' for the first time. The Owner in the doorway, hearing it.

panels.composition: The backroom: foam core sheets, a cutting table, a dull utility knife. WOOD cutting, the blade dragging. Rain in vertical hatching through a small window.

balloons.text: Art school is a commercial racket designed to castrate raw vision.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a young man in a frame shop's backroom dragging a dull utility knife through foam core on a cutting table, rain hatched through a small window

panels.composition: The knife tearing the foam instead of cutting it. A ragged edge.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, close-up of a dull utility knife tearing a ragged edge in white foam core

panels.composition: The OWNER in the doorway, glasses on a cord, a fresh blade in her fingers, held out.

balloons.text: Raw vision needs a sharp blade, Arthur. Everything does.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, an older woman with glasses on a cord standing in a doorway holding out a fresh utility blade between two fingers
image.notes: The owner's first 'Arthur' (see characters.md: Jan 2001 is her first in the book's order; this one is earlier — update: Oct 2000, the blade).

panels.composition: Wood taking the blade. The cut, clean. The word 'racket' in a small balloon, said to nobody, quieter.
